boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (120th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 2 features for Montana, measured 2026-11-12. Layer 4, the 119th Congress's map, draws the same 2 districts (every intersection-over-union 1.0), so nothing changes on 3 January 2027, and the builder refuses to write if the two differ before then. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 50 features, measured 2026-11-12, identical to the 2024 vintage (layer 5) that day. Senate District N is exactly House Districts 2N-1 and 2N (measured that day on TIGERweb's own polygons), so both chambers are simplified in one shared topology and their lines cannot part. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: mt-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from Open States' export of current legislators, compiled from the Legislature's own pages, because the Legislature's own directory (legislators.legmt.gov) already carried the terms that begin in January beside the members they succeed on 2026-11-12, 154 records for 150 seats, so it could not say who sits today (Adam's choice of 2026-11-10: the legislature's own site first, Open States as the fallback): each senator's name, party, e-mail address at legmt.gov and page on the Legislature's site, and nothing at any other domain.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 56 features, measured 2026-11-12. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Each Montana county is governed by an elected board of county commissioners, and also elects officers such as a clerk and recorder, a treasurer, a sheriff and a county attorney. Butte-Silver Bow and Anaconda-Deer Lodge are each a city and a county in one consolidated government. No list of them was read in this pass, so the card says how the county is governed and names nobody. Recorded as gap mt-county-officials.

layers.label: School District (Secondary)
layers.rank_note: 97 secondary districts, about 2,561 km2 of land on average, running the higher grades over the same ground as the elementary districts, drawn from a mirrored tile archive

source.answers: The secondary school district covering the point, where one runs the higher grades over the point's elementary district.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 1 (secondary school districts), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 97 features for Montana, measured 2026-11-12: every one running grades 9 to 12. The unified districts and the elementary districts together cover the state's land (128,588 and 248,385 km2 of Montana's 376,974 km2), and the 97 secondary districts lie over the same ground as the elementary districts, so a reader there is in one elementary and one secondary district at once.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No list of the districts' school board members was read in this pass — recorded as gap mt-school-board-members.
source.applies: Montana — the same ground as the elementary districts; the layer answers nothing elsewhere.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 373 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas that reach into Montana (476 in the app's bounding box), about 1,011 km2 of land on average, drawn from a tile archive of the ones inside the state; the layer hides outside it

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, mirrored into a vector-tile archive of the ZCTAs that reach into Montana (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py). ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='30'. The app's box reaches into Idaho, Wyoming, South Dakota and North Dakota, and measured 2026-11-12, 373 of the 476 ZCTAs in it reach into Montana and are kept in the archive.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Montana. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code.

layers.label: City or Town
layers.rank_note: 127 incorporated cities and towns, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The incorporated city or town containing the point, or that the point is outside every one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 127 records: 73 towns, 52 cities, the balance of Butte-Silver Bow and Anaconda-Deer Lodge County, the last two each a city and a county in one consolidated government, measured 2026-11-12. MOST OF MONTANA IS IN NO INCORPORATED CITY OR TOWN (about 1% of its land, 4,572.2 of 376,973.5 km2, is inside one), and there the county is the general-purpose local government, so an empty card says the point is outside every one rather than naming a place. Butte-Silver Bow and Anaconda-Deer Lodge are each a city and a county in one consolidated government, which the Census draws as a place, and their cards say so. The Census's census-designated places and county subdivisions are statistical areas with no government and are not drawn.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No statewide roster of Montana's local officials was read in this pass; the card names the place and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap mt-municipal-officeholders.

layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-11-12: 145 points in Montana's envelope, which reaches into Idaho, Wyoming, South Dakota and North Dakota; the service caps a page at 2,000 records, so the loader pages if that is ever reached.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Montana — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: Montana State Capitol, 1301 East 6th Avenue, Helena, Lewis and Clark County

negative_point.note: Saskatchewan, Canada, north of the Montana line — outside Montana and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-11-12: TIGERweb's state layer names no state here, because it is in Canada (control: the Montana State Capitol returns Montana), none of the state's shipped boundary files contains it, and no outline in fleet-outlines.json does, nor any outline in the change that opens the last thirteen states. IT IS IN CANADA, SO NO NEIGHBOUR'S GO-LIVE MOVES IT.

geometry.note: The whole-Montana outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from the county fabric (56 counties).
Montana's 56 counties — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The 2 U.S. House districts, TIGERweb layer 0 (CD120), the same map as layer 4 (CD119).
The 50 Montana Senate districts, TIGERweb layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper), simplified in one topology with the House districts.
The 100 Montana House districts, TIGERweb layer 2 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Lower), simplified in one topology with the Senate districts.

The ZIP code search index (scripts/build_zip_index.mjs): one Point per ZIP code the app's ZIP layer draws, at the spot inside it on the layer's own ground farthest from every edge, with its extent and its layer, so a ZIP code typed into the search box selects that spot, turns the ZIP layer on and pins it for comparison (ENGINE geocoder-search, showZip). A ZIP code with no spot 75 m clear of every edge is left out, and one that crosses into another app's state is listed by whichever app holds more of it. GENERATED from data/app/tiles/zip-code.pmtiles, with each spot inside metro-outline.json (the outline its coverage test reads); --check rebuilds it from the committed archive and outline. Exact count, because it changes only when the Census Bureau changes its ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, and that wants reading rather than a widened bound.

The officers Montana elects statewide and its two U.S. senators: state, officers (office, name, the office's own website, the day the name was last checked there) and usSenate. Built weekly by scripts/build_statewide_officials.py from mt/data/source/statewide-officials.source.json, which lists each office, the name and the page that must print it; the build reads robots.txt before every page, refuses to write when a page it read no longer prints the name, keeps the last checked record when a page cannot be read, and takes the senators from senate.gov's own list. Network-first: a name can change.
